name: Test-time adaptation (TTA) using the known heel prefix: label-driven TTA for time-series forecasting (TAFAS, AAAI 2025; PETSA, ICML 2025 TTA workshop; FAC 'principled TTA' 2026), test-time training modules (TTL/TTT for forecasting, arXiv 2409.14012), online self-adaptive stereo (MADNet/MAD, CVPR 2019), entropy-based TTA (Tent) as a counter-example, and closed-form per-well offset / slope / gain correction (10th-place ROGII heel-anchored gain)

Oliveira, Saghar Irandoust (RBC Borealis). FAC: Haochun Wang, Ruichen Xu, Georgios Kementzidis, Karen Cho, Sebastian Ramirez Villarreal, Yuefan Deng (Stony Brook [uncertain affiliation]). MADNet: A. ROGII 10th place team (Kaggle writeup 'A compass, not a map').

venue_link: TAFAS, AAAI 2025, arXiv:2501.04970 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.04970); PETSA, ICML 2025 Workshop on Test-Time Adaptation, arXiv:2506.23424 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.23424); FAC 'Towards Principled Test-Time Adaptation for Time Series Forecasting', arXiv:2605.17250 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17250); TTL 'Test Time Learning for Time Series Forecasting', arXiv:2409.14012 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.14012); MADNet 'Real-time self-adaptive deep stereo', CVPR 2019, arXiv:1810.05424 (https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2019/html/Tonioni_Real-Time_Self-Adaptive_Deep_Stereo_CVPR_2019_paper.html); Tent, ICLR 2021, arXiv:2006.10726; ROGII 10th place: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rogii-wellbore-geology-prediction/writeups/10th-place-solution-a-compass-not-a-map
code_availability: Public: TAFAS https://github.com/kimanki/TAFAS ; PETSA https://github.com/BorealisAI/PETSA ; MADNet https://github.com/CVLAB-Unibo/Real-time-self-adaptive-deep-stereo ; Tent https://github.com/DequanWang/tent. FAC: code not verified [uncertain]. The pseudo-heel mechanism needed for us already exists in our repo: Simulator.start_point_shift in kaggle_1st_place/solution/experiments/arch/seq_NN_dataset.py (disabled by default, aug_cfg['start_point_shift']['apply_prob']=0.0).
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed for TAFAS (AAAI), MADNet (CVPR), Tent (ICLR); workshop paper for PETSA; arXiv preprints for FAC and TTL; ROGII numbers are competition writeups (read via our A17 extraction; the Kaggle pages are JS-rendered and could not be re-fetched here). Plus an internal diagnostic run for this report on results/baseline_check/holdout_predictions.pqt (60-epoch baseline, 155 wells, pooled 5.43 ft): a global heel-anchored gain is flat (optimum s=1.00), and offset transfer only works WITHIN a suffix (see metric_and_performance). No geosteering-specific TTA paper found.
extreme_summary: Label-driven TTA freezes the trained model and fits a tiny calibration module (TAFAS gated input/output calibration, PETSA low-rank gated adapters) to ground truth that has already been revealed for part of the current series, giving about 2-10% MSE gains on non-stationary forecasting benchmarks. For us the revealed labels are the heel prefix (~1,700 ft median), so the transferable recipe is: move the heel back inside the known prefix (pseudo-heels), predict the known part, and fit either a closed-form correction or a few adapter / BN steps per well before predicting the real suffix; entropy-minimisation TTA (Tent) is mode-seeking and should be avoided under an RMSE-expectation decode.
task_definition: Adapt a pretrained predictor at inference time to the particular test series using information available only then. Forecasting TTA (TAFAS, PETSA, FAC): multivariate forecasting under distribution shift, with the first p steps of the forecast window revealed before the rest (partially observed ground truth, POGT). MADNet: continuous self-supervised adaptation of a stereo network to a new domain from photometric reprojection loss. For us: predict TVT over the unknown suffix of one lateral given its GR, trajectory, typewell and the known TVT over the heel prefix; the adaptation signal is the prefix TVT labels (and optionally prefix GR-typewell self-consistency).
inputs: Forecasting TTA: look-back window X plus revealed partial targets Y[:p]. MADNet: stereo pairs only (unsupervised). Ours: the unchanged 16-channel cost image plus, for TTA, K pseudo-heel versions of the same well built by shifting the prefix/suffix boundary back by D in the known prefix (so that the prefix labels become pseudo-suffix targets).
target_parameterisation: Forecasting TTA works on the raw target (MSE/Huber) or its spectrum (PETSA frequency loss, FAC frequency-domain correction). For us: the per-column TVT expectation (or per-column posterior over 400 levels); closed-form corrections parameterise the correction as offset + slope in MD (drift in the surface A = TVT + Z, see A18) or as a heel-anchored gain s on (TVT_pred - TVT_heel).
output_representation: Point forecasts corrected by an additive calibration term (TAFAS/PETSA output GCM: Y_hat + tanh(alpha) * (W Y_hat + b)). For us the posterior can be shifted (a per-well shift or per-column shift of the 400-level softmax, which preserves the expectation decode) or re-tempered.
architecture: TAFAS: frozen source forecaster wrapped by an input Gated Calibration Module GCM(X) = X + tanh(alpha) * (W X + b) and an output GCM of the same form, with W, b zero-initialised so adaptation starts as a no-op; only W, b, alpha are updated. PETSA: same placement, W factorised low-rank (A B) and gating tanh(alpha * X) input-dependent, about 33x less memory than TAFAS at window 720. FAC: correction parameterised directly in the frequency domain. TTL (2409.14012): replaces Mamba blocks with Test-Time-Training layers whose hidden state is updated by a self-supervised inner loss per sequence (no labels). MADNet/MAD: lightweight pyramid stereo network; MAD updates one sub-module per frame chosen by a reward, making online backprop real-time. Tent: updates BatchNorm affine parameters to minimise prediction entropy.
core_mechanism: Partial ground truth is the most reliable adaptation signal available in forecasting: TAFAS uses L_partial = MSE(Y_cali[:p], Y[:p]) on the revealed prefix of the current window plus L_full on earlier fully-revealed windows, and chooses p by the dominant FFT period (PAAS). Freezing the backbone and learning only a zero-initialised, gated correction keeps the source semantics and prevents the few revealed points from overfitting the whole model. The key question for any transfer is whether the error on the revealed part is informative about the error on the part still to predict. In forecasting that holds because the shift is in the series statistics; in our task the model is re-anchored to the true TVT at the heel, so errors restart near zero and grow like a random walk (10th place: mean |err| 0.32 ft at 50 ft to 4.55 ft at 5,000 ft; first fifth of the scored zone predicts the last fifth with r = 0.131). Therefore the transferable part is per-WELL systematic bias (typewell-lateral GR mismatch, stretch, dip-bias of this well), measured by forecasting inside the prefix from pseudo-heels, not per-window persistence.
training_objective: TAFAS: L_partial + L_full (MSE). PETSA: Huber (delta 0.5) + frequency (FFT spectrum) loss + patch-wise structural loss (local mean/variance/correlation), each on partial and delayed-full labels. Tent: entropy minimisation (label-free). MADNet: photometric reprojection loss (label-free). For us, candidate TTA losses on pseudo-heel forecasts: MSE of the expectation vs prefix TVT (RMSE-consistent) plus the existing soft CE to the typewell targets; avoid pure entropy minimisation.
decoding: Unchanged: after adaptation the forecaster produces its usual output (for us: posterior expectation, optionally MD-phase TTA x8).
metric_consistent_decode: Label-driven TTA with an MSE/expectation loss keeps the decode RMSE-consistent. Tent-style entropy minimisation sharpens posteriors toward the dominant mode (mode-seeking) and is expected to raise pooled RMSE on bimodal (repeated-band) wells, where our hedged expectation is Bayes-optimal.
evidence_scope: Single series / single well: the adapter is fit per test series (or continuously across a stream). For us: one well plus its typewell; pseudo-heels reuse the same well's prefix.
prefix_conditioning: This item IS prefix conditioning. Forecasting TTA: fine-tunes a calibration module on revealed ground truth. Our current pipeline already uses the prefix in three closed ways: (1) seen_tvt_rel and tw_seen_tvt_abs_diff input channels; (2) GR_calibration (typewell_calibration_with_seen=True) blends the typewell GR toward a pseudo-curve built from prefix (TVT_input, GR) within TVT0 +- 100 ft with weight 0.7 -- a closed-form test-time calibration of the reference; (3) the prediction is anchored at the heel TVT. What is missing: any use of the prefix LABELS as a supervised adaptation signal for the network or its output (fine-tuning, offset/slope/temperature fitted per well).
propose_vs_select: Single adapted output; can slot in as a per-well post-processor applied to any member (ConvNeXt, FastViT, AnchorCNN) or produce an adapted copy of a member for blending.
physical_constraints: None intrinsic. For us a correction restricted to offset + slope of the surface A(MD) = TVT + Z is physically interpretable (constant dip bias); slope extrapolation must be heavily shrunk (see risk).
dataset: TAFAS/PETSA/FAC: ETTh1/ETTh2/ETTm1/ETTm2, Weather, Electricity, Traffic, Exchange, etc. (standard long-horizon forecasting benchmarks). MADNet: KITTI, synthetic-to-real stereo sequences. Ours: 773 Kaggle wells (618 train / 155 holdout), known prefix median 1,702 ft (q10 1,422, q90 1,944 ft of MD from the first row, measured here from data/train), unknown suffix median 4,840 ft (q10 3,263, q90 6,349 ft).
synthetic_to_real: TTA is a sim-to-real tool in stereo (MADNet adapts synthetic-trained networks online to real scenes). For us it could absorb per-well synthetic-to-real mismatch (85% synthetic training), since the adapter only sees real prefix labels of the test well.
metric_and_performance: TAFAS (Table 1): average MSE gains ~4.95% (iTransformer) and 5.20% (DLinear) at H=336, 5.76% and 6.30% at H=720; up to 45% on Chronos on unseen data; ablation iTransformer H=720: 0.786 no-TTA -> 0.704 full TAFAS; removing GCM 0.832 (worse than no TTA), output-only calibration 0.808. PETSA: ~2-5% average MSE reduction vs no-TTA; 127 best-MSE wins vs TAFAS 88; e.g. ETTh1 iTransformer 0.449 -> 0.432 (TAFAS 0.435); ~33.6x less memory. ROGII (via A17): 10th place applied a heel-anchored gain s = 1.024 at the end of its stack; drift extrapolation from the prefix 12.60 vs flat 15.91 (their scale); 22nd: OOF drift-direction correctors CV -0.25 but LB +0.34. Internal diagnostic on our 60-epoch baseline (pooled 5.431 ft): global heel-anchored gain s in {0.97..1.05} gives 5.442/5.431/5.431/5.434/5.442/5.453/5.486 -- flat, optimum 1.00, so the 10th-place gain does not transfer; using the first 20% of each SUFFIX as if revealed, a constant offset (mean error of its last 50 rows) lowers the RMSE of the remaining 80% from 5.92 to 5.51 ft (first 30%: 6.13 -> 5.60), whereas slope extrapolation explodes (12.8 ft); correlation of early vs late mean error 0.20 / 0.42 / 0.53 for 10/20/30% -- i.e. errors are persistent once they exist, but the prefix itself carries no suffix error because the prediction is re-anchored at the heel.
comparability: Forecasting-benchmark MSE percentages are not comparable to pooled RMSE on 155 wells. The internal diagnostic is directly comparable but uses suffix labels (an upper-bound style probe, not a deployable method).
validation_protocol: TAFAS/PETSA use online streams with delayed labels; FAC argues protocols are heterogeneous and some leak (evaluating on steps already used for updates) and proposes a matured-ground-truth-only protocol. For us: TTA must use only prefix labels of each holdout well; any hyperparameter (D, steps, lr, shrinkage) must be tuned on training wells (or cross-fitted halves of the holdout) to avoid holdout tuning.
inference_budget: Closed-form correction: K extra forward passes per well (K pseudo-heels, e.g. 4) -> ~4 x 22 ms (FastViT tiny) on GPU. Adapter / BN fine-tuning: ~5-20 forward+backward steps per well on K pseudo-heel crops -> roughly 0.3-1.5 s per well on the RTX 5060 [uncertain]; fits Kaggle / rig budgets (seconds per well).
repeated_layers: Weak lever. Prefix labels tell the model which band the heel is in (already used via the anchor). A per-well adapter fitted on pseudo-heels could learn that for this well the lateral GR systematically matches the band above/below (e.g. a GR scale/offset mismatch vs the typewell), which is one cause of wrong-band picks. Entropy-based TTA would make band confusion worse by committing to one mode.
drift: Main target. Drift = one straight-line error per well (~25% of our squared error; per-well line oracle 3.08 ft on ep150). A per-well dip-bias estimated from pseudo-heel forecasts inside the prefix (predict prefix segments, measure the slope of error in A-space) could be applied, shrunk, to the suffix. External evidence is pessimistic: 10th and 22nd found drift direction essentially unpredictable from observables, and our diagnostic shows naive slope extrapolation is catastrophic; an offset correction helps only once error has accumulated, which never happens in the prefix.
uncertainty_and_calibration: Pseudo-heel forecasts give a per-well calibration check: compare predicted posterior spread against realised error on known prefix segments and fit a per-well temperature (or a shrunk global-plus-well temperature) -- a label-driven, per-well version of B09 temperature scaling that keeps the expectation decode. No TTA paper reports calibration of histogram outputs.
where_to_use: A post-processing / inference stage between the trained model and seq_NN_holdout_eval.py (or seq_NN_rescore.py, which already rescored MD-phase TTA without retraining): for each well build K pseudo-heel items by moving the boundary back inside the prefix (reuse Simulator.start_point_shift logic deterministically, plus _recalibrate_typewell_after_start_shift so GR_calibration only sees the pseudo-prefix), predict, compare with known TVT, then (a) closed-form: offset / shrunk-slope / temperature correction; or (b) gradient TTA: zero-initialised output calibration head (TAFAS-style GCM on the 400-level logits or on the expectation) or BN-affine / last-decoder-block update for a few steps; then predict the real suffix.
error_mode_targeted: Drift (~25%) primarily; per-well calibration (broad/skewed humps ~13%, blend 15%) secondarily; band confusion only indirectly (per-well GR mismatch).
gap_vs_our_implementation: We already do: prefix as input channels (seen_tvt_rel, tw_seen_tvt_abs_diff), closed-form reference calibration from the prefix (GR_calibration, weight 0.7 within TVT0 +- 100 ft), heel anchoring, MD-phase TTA x8 (test-time augmentation, not adaptation; -0.04 to -0.15 ft, 4/4 positive), and a start_point_shift augmentation that is switched off. We do NOT: (1) use prefix TVT labels as a supervised signal at inference -- no pseudo-heel forecasting, no per-well fine-tuning, no per-well output calibration; (2) estimate per-well bias or temperature from the model's own behaviour on the known part; (3) train the model to be adaptable (start_point_shift off means the network has only ever seen the true heel position, so pseudo-heel predictions may be slightly out of distribution). The 10th-place global heel gain (s=1.024) is NOT a gap: our diagnostic shows the optimum is s=1.00 for our model.
proposed_experiment: E0 (zero training, go/no-go, ~1 h): new script kaggle_1st_place/solution/seq_NN_pseudo_heel.py that loads a trained run (models.pkl via the seq_NN_rescore.py loader), and for each of the 155 holdout wells builds K=4 pseudo-heel items with the boundary moved back by D in {300, 600, 900, 1200} ft inside the known prefix (deterministic version of Simulator.start_point_shift; typewell recalibrated on the pseudo-prefix only). Record per-well pseudo-forecast error features: mean error, error slope in A = TVT + Z per 1,000 ft, error at the pseudo-suffix end, and posterior spread vs |error|. Then correlate them with the real suffix error (mean error, fitted line slope) per well. Go only if Spearman |rho| >= 0.3 on the slope or offset (cross-fitted); otherwise stop -- this mirrors the 10th/22nd 'drift is an info wall' finding at no cost. E1 (closed-form, if E0 passes): correct the suffix by beta * (estimated A-space slope) * (MD - MD_heel) with beta fitted by cross-fitting on holdout halves (or on training-well OOF), plus an optional per-well temperature tau_w = clip(global_tau * f(spread ratio)); control = same weights without correction; score with seq_NN_robust_compare.py (paired bootstrap, k*). E2 (gradient TTA): TAFAS-style zero-initialised output GCM on the per-column logits (a per-well shift + scale along the level axis, 2-10 params) or BN affine of the decoder, optimised 10 steps Adam lr 1e-3 on the K pseudo-heel items with loss = MSE(expectation, prefix TVT) + existing soft CE; control = no TTA. E3 (make the model adaptable): retrain one 150-epoch run with aug_cfg['start_point_shift']['apply_prob']=0.25 so pseudo-heels are in distribution, then repeat E0-E2; control = baseline 150-epoch run (also tells whether start_point_shift alone helps as augmentation).
implementation_effort: E0 low (one script reusing rescore loader and start_point_shift; ~150 lines). E1 low. E2 medium (per-well autograd loop, careful BN handling: freeze running stats). E3 low code, one 150-epoch training (~5 h).
gpu_cost: E0/E1: inference only, K=4 extra passes on 155 wells, minutes on the RTX 5060 8 GB. E2: ~10 forward+backward steps per well on 4 crops, a few minutes for 155 wells with FastViT, ~10-20 min with ConvNeXt-small [uncertain]. E3: one standard 150-epoch run (~5 h).
distillation_compatibility: Fully compatible: closed-form and output-calibration TTA act after the student; BN/adapter TTA works on the FastViT student equally (it has BN). The teacher does not need to change.
error_correlation_with_ours: Not a new member; it modifies the error of an existing member per well. If it works, it corrects exactly the component the ensemble cannot average away (shared per-well drift), so its benefit should survive blending.
risk: (1) Information wall: the prefix error is near zero by construction (re-anchoring), and external evidence (10th r = 0.131 early-vs-late, 22nd drift correctors LB +0.34) plus our diagnostic (slope extrapolation 5.9 -> 12.8 ft) say per-well drift direction is barely predictable; pseudo-heel forecasts are short (300-1,200 ft) where drift has not yet accumulated. (2) Pseudo-heels inside the build/curve section may be unrepresentative of the lateral (prefix includes the landing section [uncertain]). (3) Overfitting a per-well adapter to ~1,000 ft of labels; need zero-init gating and heavy shrinkage. (4) Tent-style entropy TTA is mode-seeking and would raise RMSE on bimodal wells. (5) Effect sizes of a few tenths of a foot are at our +-0.39 ft single-comparison noise floor; use paired bootstrap and cross-fitting. (6) GR_calibration already absorbs the easiest per-well bias (typewell GR offset/scale), so the remaining transferable bias may be small.
notes: Why forecasting TTA works and ours may not: TAFAS/PETSA exploit persistence of error within one forecast window (the first p steps of the SAME window), which our diagnostic confirms exists within a suffix (offset from first 20% cuts late RMSE 5.92 -> 5.51) but is unavailable at test time because nothing in the suffix is revealed. The only analogue is a rig setting where labels arrive progressively while drilling (real-time geosteering): there, TAFAS-style partial-truth adaptation is directly applicable and the gain could be large -- worth noting for the thesis framing even though the Kaggle protocol hides it. Related items: B09 (calibration), A15/A18 (dip state, A-space), A17 (10th/22nd drift findings), B11 (start_point_shift as augmentation). TTL (2409.14012) is test-time TRAINING layers inside the architecture (self-supervised inner loop, no labels), only loosely related.
